title: KB3i: the 18-point cover remainder for F2^7 - parity shortcut DEMOTED, m=5 obstruction localized (outcome=partial, no new kappa)
body:
# KB3i: the 18-point cover remainder for F2^7 - parity shortcut DEMOTED, m=5 obstruction localized (outcome=partial, no new kappa)

Contributor: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance in scoping, implementation, verification and writing; no model named; no independent human review claimed). No kappa, supplier, certificate or selected-frontier change.

## Change and mathematical scope

In the PR943 prefix-walk model ([PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943) by Ross Richardson) a restored seven-source singleton word is universal exactly when its prefix set `P` covers: `P + P = F2^7`. The 17-point question is closed ([PR 2542](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2542), [PR 2634](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2634), [PR 2773](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2773), [PR 2870](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2870)); [PR 2911](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2911) narrowed the 18-point question to the splits `(12,6)`, `(11,7)`, `(10,8)`, `(9,9)` and proved that any `(12,6)` or `(10,8)` cover must have a vanishing character off the all-ones hyperplane; [PR 2933](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2933) classified the vanishing configurations and recorded the class floors; [PR 2961](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2961) decided the three tightest classes and fully excluded `(10,8)`; [PR 3023](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3023) killed `(12,6)` A-vanish `(5,1)` and recorded the remainder this PR takes: **the surviving `(12,6)` A-vanish classes `(4,2)`, `(3,3)` plus the both-odd splits `(11,7)`, `(9,9)`, which carry no vanishing character.** This PR is strictly SET-level: no words are enumerated.

Record chain authors, all verified against current ground truth with `gh pr view NNN --json author,title` at writing: PR 2542/2634/2773/2870/2911/2933/2961/3023 are Aaron Wang (navinor); [PR 2691](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2691) and [PR 2973](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2973) are Nicholas Stone (NicholasStone); [PR 3005](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3005) is Nick Petalas (petalas); [PR 1185](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1185) is Mister-Meeseeks.

Concurrent word-level state, recorded honestly: PR 2973 (merged) corrected a false-prune defect in the word-census budgets and records `22 <= f(7) <= 24`; PR 3005 independently corroborates it. PR 2973's own scope note records the set-level chain PR 2773-3023 as unaffected. Under `22 <= f(7) <= 24` this PR's question is the deciding necessary condition for `f(7) = 22`: if no 18-point set covers `F2^7`, every universal word at `L = 22` needs at least 19 distinct prefixes.

## Verdict per class (exact integers)

| Split | Class | PR 2933 floor | Status here | Deciding evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (12,6) | A-vanish (4,2) | 44 >= 32 | NOT decided (walk-ready) | exact reduction `D1 = {0,1}` under `GL(5,2)`, budgets 20/20/24; walk too large |
| (12,6) | A-vanish (3,3) | 45 >= 32 | NOT decided (walk-ready) | four L3 lines direct, all budgets slack, no forced structure |
| (11,7) | both-odd, no vanishing char | - | NOT excluded; parity shortcut DEMOTED | both-odd covers exist at m=3 (complete census); frontier `E_o = 13`, `min sum rho^2 = 17` |
| (9,9) | both-odd, no vanishing char | - | NOT excluded; parity shortcut DEMOTED | both-odd covers exist at m=3 (complete census); frontier `E_o = 17`, `min sum rho^2 = 19` |

No class is decided here. The `(4,2)`/`(3,3)` reductions and budgets are necessary conditions and exact finite search domains (PR 3023's classification, reproduced), not exclusions.

## Route (b): the parity shortcut is PROVEN false (DEMOTED)

The cleanest way to break `(11,7)`/`(9,9)` would be a parity rule: a covering reduced pair `(A,B)` of `F2^m` (i.e. `A + B = F2^m` and `(A+A) u (B+B) = F2^m`) must have `|A|` and `|B|` both even. Then the both-odd splits `(11,7)`/`(9,9)` would be excluded and the 18-point question would collapse to `(12,6)`/`(10,8)`.

**This is false.** A complete enumeration of the reduced covering problem in `F2^3` (all `2^8 x 2^8` subset pairs) finds covering pairs in every both-odd split `(3,5)`, `(3,7)`, `(5,3)`, `(5,5)`, `(5,7)`, `(7,3)`, `(7,5)`, `(7,7)` - for example `(5,5)` has 3136 covers and `(7,7)` has 64. So there is no dimension-free parity obstruction, and none can be used to kill `(11,7)`/`(9,9)`. (Among small both-odd splits only `(3,3)` is empty.) This is a PROVEN negative on the shortcut, not on the splits themselves.

## The m=5 ground truth and its obstruction (route b, "why at m=5")

The recorded ground truth - `F2^5` covers exist only in splits `(2,8)`, `(4,6)`, `(6,4)`, `(8,2)` - is a statement about the reduced problem in `F2^4` with `|A| + |B| = 10`. It is confirmed by complete enumeration, and the both-odd emptiness is localized to three distinct mechanisms:

| m=4 split | covers | why empty (both-odd) |
|---|---|---|
| (2,8) | 15360 (even) | - (witness `A=[0,1] B=[0,2,4,6,8,10,12,15]`) |
| (4,6) | 143360 (even) | - (witness `A=[0,1,2,3] B=[0,1,2,4,8,15]`) |
| (1,9) | 0 | counting: `st = 9 < 16`, so `A+B` never covers (self covers for all 183040 pairs) |
| (3,7) | 0 | cross never covers: `st = 21 >= 16` but `A+B != F2^4` for every pair |
| (5,5) | 0 | self never covers when cross covers: all 4085760 cross-covering pairs have `|A+A|,|B+B|` in `{8,11}` and self-union `<= 15 < 16` |

So the "even-splits-only" pattern at m=5 is a genuine fact, but its mechanism is split- and scale-specific (counting / cross / self), not a parity rule. Because both-odd covers exist at m=3 and the `(5,5)` self-sum bound is scale-dependent, the m=5 obstruction does not lift to a valid exclusion of `(11,7)`/`(9,9)` at m=6. No parity or self-sum-size argument is available there. (DEMOTED: the lift.)

## The (11,7)/(9,9) identity frontier (reproduced, quantified)

Both splits survive the rho^2/identity layer; the exact remaining conditions (PR 2961's, reproduced here) are:

| Split | odd excess `E_o` | even-half bound | min `sum rho^2` (partition) | effective min (post PR 2961) | squeeze (opposite-parity) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (11,7) | 13 | 42 | 13 | 17 (all-ones and `(2,1^11)` excluded) | inapplicable (`s+t` even) |
| (9,9) | 17 | 34 | 17 | 19 (all-ones excluded) | inapplicable (`s+t` even) |

`E_o = s*t - 64`; the even-half bound is the max of `f_hat^2 + g_hat^2` off the all-ones hyperplane from the self-sum half of coverage (`s + t + 2*P - 128`, `P = C(s,2)+C(t,2)`). The PR 2870 Parseval squeeze uses only odd coverage and requires opposite parity; its hypothesis fails for every 18-point split (all have `s + t = 18` even), so its deficit argument reaches no contradiction here. Breaking `(11,7)`/`(9,9)` requires pushing the even-half (self-sum) coverage multiplicities at the 501/196 surviving rows (PR 2911) - the direction PR 2870 did not use. This is PR 2961's open question 2, untouched by any prior PR and not settled here.

## Route (c): bounded construction search (no cover found)

A bounded, seeded local search finds no covering 18-set:

| search | best coverage | record ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| direct `k=18` on `F2^7` (3 seeds) | 118 / 128 | 119 / 128 (PR 2634) |
| reduced `(12,6)`, `(11,7)`, `(10,8)` on `F2^6` | 118 / 128 | - |
| reduced `(9,9)` on `F2^6` | 117 / 128 | - |

Seed-invariant best 118/128; no cover reached. A failed bounded search is a scoped search failure, never an exclusion. The search ceiling is unchanged.

The light anchors are recomputed live from the byte-vendored engines; the heavy walk anchors (CLASS82/CLASS60/AV51) are read back from PR 3023's per-shard receipts (PR 3023 re-walked them from empty receipts; reproduced values match exactly).

## Reproduce

Standard library only, CPython 3.12, from the repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-remainder-kb3i-a1/verify.py quick
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-remainder-kb3i-a1/verify.py full
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-remainder-kb3i-a1/verify.py search
```

Expected markers: `PASS_KB3I_QUICK`, `PASS_KB3I_FULL`, `PASS_KB3I_SEARCH`. `quick` reproduces the anchors, the complete m=3 parity-demotion census and the `(11,7)`/`(9,9)` frontier in well under a second; `full` re-runs the complete m=4 sum-10 censuses and the `(5,5)` self-obstruction localization (271 s); `search` re-runs the bounded construction search. Registered replay: `python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/f7-18point-remainder-kb3i-a1 --check-only` passes `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`.

## Scope and limitations

Set-level only inside PR943's abstract interface. Not checked: anything word-level (PR 2973/PR 3005's corrected word census and `L = 22` versus `L = 24` are word-level work, untouched here), walk-realizability of any cover, and any kappa, supplier, tariff or selected-frontier implication. `(4,2)`, `(3,3)`, `(11,7)`, `(9,9)` are all undecided here; nothing in this PR excludes any of them, and the parity-shortcut demotion is a negative result about the method, not about the splits. No construction search found a cover (route c is a scoped search failure, not an exclusion). The recorded set-level search ceilings stay `118/128` at `k = 18` (this run) / `119/128` (PR 2634) and `124/128` at `k = 19`. All arithmetic is exact Python integers (int bitmasks); no floats are used. Frozen predecessor packages are unchanged; the six vendored engines are byte-exact with SHA-256 pins.

## Open next questions

1. **Push the even-half (self-sum) coverage identity for (11,7)/(9,9)** (PR 2961's open question 2): derive the self-sum multiplicities at the 501/196 surviving rows and check them against every cover of `F2^5` (PR 2933's census) before lifting to `m = 6`. This is the one direction the PR 2870 odd-coverage squeeze did not use. Blocked by: no known cross/self coupling identity; the parity shortcut is DEMOTED.
2. **Decide (12,6) A-vanish (4,2)** with PR 3023's recorded reduced form (W 4-sets, `D1 = {0,1}`) and budgets `|U+W| >= 20`, `|V+W| >= 20`, `|U+V| >= 24`: a complete sharded walk with generous per-shard budgets and per-shard receipts. Blocked by: nothing structural; a few hours of sharded walk (strictly larger than (5,1)'s 3,049,492,320-pair walk).
3. **Decide or identify (12,6) A-vanish (3,3)** via the direct normalized walk or a cross-line multiplicity identity. Blocked by: all four line budgets are slack and no forced structure exists.
4. **Find a valid lift of the (5,5) self-sum obstruction** to (9,9): the m=4 mechanism (`|A+A| <= 11` for cross-covering `(5,5)`) is scale-dependent and fails at m=3; determine the exact `m`/split threshold, if any, at which a self-sum-size bound forbids a both-odd self cover.
